item.title: Former Hokkaido Government Office — Guide
item.description: The Former Hokkaido Government Office, affectionately nicknamed ‘Akarenga’ (‘Red Brick’), is one of Sapporo’s most beloved historic landmarks, standing grandly in the heart of the city. Completed in 1888 in an American neo-Baroque style, this imposing red-brick building — made with some 2.5 million locally-fired bricks and topped by an octagonal dome — served as the seat of Hokkaido’s government for about 80 years. It’s a striking symbol of the Meiji-era pioneer spirit and the American influence on the island’s development.

item.title: Kurashiki Ivy Square: The Ivy-Clad Cotton Mill — Guide
item.description: Ivy Square is a complex of red-brick buildings a short walk from Kurashiki’s canal, built in 1889 as a cotton-spinning mill and now almost entirely wrapped in ivy that turns green in summer and red in autumn. The mill was converted in 1974 into a hotel, restaurants, small museums and craft workshops arranged around open courtyards and a fountain. It is a reminder that Kurashiki was an industrial as well as a merchant town, and the contrast between this Western-style brick and the white Edo storehouses on the canal is a large part of the city’s character.

item.title: Iwate Bank Red Brick Building: Morioka's Meiji Landmark — Guide
item.description: The Iwate Bank Red Brick Building is one of Morioka’s best-loved landmarks — a handsome 1911 former bank designed by Kingo Tatsuno, architect of Tokyo Station, and his partner. Its red brick and white stone facade anchors the historic city centre, and the beautifully restored interior is open to visitors. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Morioka, Iwate Hours ~10:00–16:30 (closed Tue) Admission Around ¥300 (interior) Time needed About 40 min Best time Year-round What to See The red brick and white stone Meiji facade (1911).
